findings.description: Code+tests pin a boundary condition SHEET-MARK-006's text never mentions or even acknowledges: a MISSING view tab (fresh/cold-start workbook) is classified as `Ok(empty PricePass)`, never as a transport failure. This lives at the `SheetsViewClient::read_price_pass` contract boundary — the exact function whose `Err` is SHEET-MARK-006's trigger — and is pinned concretely by `runtime/tests/cold_start.rs::the_price_pass_on_a_fresh_workbook_is_empty_not_an_error` (`adapter.read_price_pass().expect("no tab yet ⇒ no marks, not an outage")`, `assert!(pass.is_empty())`). All three B runs converged on this nearly verbatim (B1: 'a missing tab is classified as "no marks yet," never as a transport/unreachable failure'; B2: 'absence of a tab is not a transport failure and must not be classified as one'; B3: SHEET-MARK-e/f, explicitly framed as a tie-break rule keyed on the adapter's missing-vs-unreachable state). SHEET-MARK-006's text gives no hint that 'transport failure' has this carve-out — it is entirely a code-side rule. (Caveat: this rule is tested one crate over, in `runtime`'s adapter via `cold_start.rs`, not in `sheets-view/tests/marks.rs` directly — still squarely about what does/doesn't count as the 'transport failure' SHEET-MARK-006 governs.)

Code+tests delineate 'transport failure' (the whole-pass abort SHEET-MARK-006 governs) as categorically distinct from, and never triggered by, the per-symbol degrade taxonomy: `PriceReading::Permanent` → immediate per-symbol `DegradeReason::Permanent` (test `permanent_error_degrades_immediately_no_prior_carry`, loop settles without exhausting `max_polls`), and still-`Transient`/absent past the bounded window (`SettleConfig::max_polls`, default 8, per `Default for SettleConfig`) → per-symbol `DegradeReason::TimedOut` or prior-carry (tests `transient_keeps_prior_mark_and_retries_degrades_only_after_window`, `no_prior_mark_stays_transient_degrades_after_window`, `settle_pass_is_bounded_by_max_polls`). None of these produce an `Err` or abort the pass. All three B runs state this taxonomy almost identically. This is weaker than finding 1: SHEET-MARK-006's silence on these adjacent per-symbol paths is arguably expected scoping (they're plausibly governed by sibling EARS IDs, not this one) rather than a genuine unstated rule, so it reads more as B correctly triangulating the boundary of '006 than as drift.

notes:
Read the real files directly (sheets-view/src/lib.rs, sheets-view/tests/marks.rs, sheets-view/src/testkit.rs, runtime/tests/cold_start.rs) rather than relying only on the A/B text. sheets-view's `read_marks` doc comment ('# Transport failure (offline) — boundary contract') nearly restates SHEET-MARK-006 verbatim, which explains why all 3 B runs converge so tightly and so accurately on the core propagate/no-partial/prior-untouched behavior — that part is faithful reconstruction, not surplus. The real code structurally guarantees 'no partial or degraded marks' by constructing `MarksProduced` only AFTER the polling loop completes (never inside it), so any `?`-triggered Err — first poll or Nth — returns before any partial `out` is built; this matches the spec exactly and none of the A or B runs mis-describe it.

A-direction: all 3 runs invent a plausible architecture (buffer-then-commit, separate runtime-owned cache/struct) but each explicitly flags these as assumptions with no spec-text basis (invented `Mark` shape, single-call vs. polling-loop fetch model, sync/no-retry). Per the classification rule, unanimous assumption-filling with no spec-text basis is not a finding — so A surfaces nothing material. Notably, none of the given files include `runtime`'s actual marks-cache implementation (only `cold_start.rs`, which covers tab-missing/bootstrap concerns, not marks retention-on-failure), so the EARS's 'runtime... retaining the last cached marks' clause could not be independently verified against real runtime code either way — an evidence gap, not a positive A-side finding.

B-direction: given source-level access (not just tests), all 3 runs surface the same real boundary/taxonomy facts with high fidelity, most notably the missing-tab-vs-transport-failure classification, which has zero basis in SHEET-MARK-006's text — that's the one clear, stable, well-evidenced surplus finding. One thing no B run called out: `read_price_pass`'s transport failure and `batch_update_view`'s publish failure both return the same `ViewError::PublishFailed` variant (there is no dedicated Transport/Unreachable variant in `sheets-view`, unlike `runtime`'s `StoreError::{TabMissing,Unreachable}` split in `store`/`cold_start.rs`) — true but minor, not raised by any run, so not counted as a finding.
